# PRD 005: procedures

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 005-procedures.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

| owner | pij-intense-herring |
| summary | Repeatable work in pij gets written down as procedures: ddocs with stable ids, steps that are commands which check their own preconditions, and everything the procedure needs stored in its own folder. A seat finds the procedure and follows it, or writes one as it goes, so what one seat learns isn't lost when it closes. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

pij has PRDs (what and why), blueprints (how it is built) and workstreams (in what order), but nothing that says how a piece of repeatable work is done. That knowledge lives in `just` recipes, AGENTS.md rules, skills and seats' memory, and is rebuilt each time. On 2026-11-23 the prime changed a live seat's reasoning effort by hand; the steps existed nowhere until written up as `docs/how/change-seat-effort.md`. osk-central built a procedure system the week before (`PROC-<area>-NNNN`, after the operator's "this is a business, not the wild west"). A survey of 8 of its seats found what worked (steps that are commands, refusals that name the fix, writing the procedure as you go) and what hurt: preconditions that lived in one person's head (6 of 8 seats), order between procedures that nobody checked, two layouts side by side, and tooling that only worked from the repo root. This PRD takes the first and designs out the second.

<a id="actors"></a>

## Actors

| id | name | need |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a-operator | operator | Repeatable work done the same way by any seat, rebuildable from the procedure alone, with the approval of each procedure on record. |
| a-prime | prime | To hand a seat the procedure for its task, and to see which work has none. |
| a-seat | seat | To find the procedure for a task, see where a run is, and be stopped with the fix when a step isn't ready. |
| a-author | author | To start a procedure in one command and write it from what actually happened. |
| a-reviewer | reviewer | To check what a step does, not what someone says it did, and to see drift without reading every file. |

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | Any seat can do a repeatable job from its procedure alone; deleting the result and rebuilding it from the procedure works. |
| g-2 | A step cannot run when its preconditions aren't met, and says what to run first. |
| g-3 | Everything that belongs to a procedure is stored with it, and everything it relies on elsewhere is linked. |
| g-4 | Procedures stay joined to PRDs, blueprints and recipes, and drift is caught by `harness checks`. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| n-1 | A formal precondition language. Preconditions are commands that pass or fail. |
| n-2 | Managing secrets. pij keeps no vault; a procedure that needs a secret uses the tool that holds it. |
| n-3 | Migrating osk-central's procedures, or enforcing procedures in other projects. |
| n-4 | Replacing `just`, `harness checks` or skills. Procedures call them. |
| n-5 | A hand-kept index of procedures. |
